newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends higher, jump-started by NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends higher, jump-started by NYMEX.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices ended slightly higher on Wednesday in a quiet market that was jump-started by a sharp rally in NYMEX crude and gasoline futures, traders said.
A one-cent-a-gallon rise in NYMEX gasoline and another round of inventory reports showing tight U.S. supplies, underpinned NWE prices, they said.
"Certainly the arb is still there but only if you've got just the right ship or have big volumes," said one London trader.
"Tight is not the right word," for the NWE market, he said. "There is not an overhang but it is quite adequately supplied."
"People are starting to wonder when the stocks (in the U.S.) will be built and if not, then the further out you go it will certainly get interesting," he said.
Eurograde barges rose $2 to $218/$220 fob ARA in thin dealings, with regular unleaded barely traded to end at $213/$215 fob ARA.

Gasoline prices jumped higher in part, traders said, to Tuesday's American Petroleum Institute report that showed U.S. gasoline inventories were 11.0 million barrels below a year ago, despite a week-on-week increase of 3.7 million.
Today's Energy Information Administration report from the government showed a smaller build of 2.1 million, but the year-ago deficit was narrower at 7.3 million.
